item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q008_v1_atp_synthase_bulge_classification","answer":"The bulge domain shares the barrel-sandwich architecture—a sandwich of half-barrel-shaped β-sheets—but that structural resemblance does not establish common ancestry with the other superfamilies. In SCOPe 2.08 it belongs to class b (All beta proteins), fold b.84 (Barrel-sandwich hybrid; SUNID 51229), and its own superfamily b.84.5 (V1 ATP synthase A subunit, bulge domain-like; SUNID 310577). It is separate from Single hybrid motif (b.84.1), Rudiment single hybrid motif (b.84.2), Duplicated hybrid motif (b.84.3), and Ribosomal L27 protein-like (b.84.4).\n\nThis placement recognizes a homologous group within b.84.5 while withholding a supported homology claim linking it to those neighboring superfamilies. It does not prove independent origins or exclude a deeper evolutionary relationship. The more specific family b.84.5.1 (SUNID 310616) includes both V1 and A1 ATP synthase A-subunit bulge domains, expressing a closer evolutionary relationship between them. The classification concerns the bulge domain, not the entire multidomain A subunit. Neither shared fold nor membership in an ATP synthase subunit justifies transferring catalytic activity, binding specificity, or detailed template-derived features across these superfamilies; those require additional sequence, structural, and functional evidence.","evidence_used":["Pretrained knowledge of SCOPe hierarchy and homology interpretation","mcp__scope__search_scop","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","mcp__scope__list_scop_children","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=bulge&mode=auto&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310577","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310577/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51229","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51229/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51229/children?limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310616","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/310616/children?limit=20"]}]}
